key_insight: An adsorbate-free graph neural network screens dissociative water adsorption on nickel using only bare-metal geometry and candidate binding-site anchors.
engineering_relevance: The approach reduces reliance on exhaustive DFT screening and scales to nickel nanoparticles containing approximately 3,000 atoms.
method: Define candidate O- and H-binding sites as sets of nickel anchor atoms.
Build local graphs from anchors and their surrounding MACE-relaxed bare nickel geometry.
Use separate GNNs to predict adsorption energy and whether binding sites survive DFT relaxation.
evidence_signal: The energy model achieved 0.031 eV internal-validation MAE, with independent tests on unseen Ni55, Ni91, Ni130 clusters and larger surface cells supporting transferability, particularly for relative-energy ranking.
watch_item: Quantitative accuracy varies across systems, so transferred predictions warrant DFT checks before relying on absolute adsorption energies.
paper_title: Adsorbate-Free Screening of Dissociative Water Adsorption on Nickel Nanoparticles via Graph Neural Networks
